    - *Player*! Welcome, welcome! Have you an opinion? Everyone has an opinion! Mine is about a bridge, and I warn you now, it is a long one. The opinion, I mean. The bridge too, if it comes to that.
    - Tonight, the iron door! I have two speeches: one for, one against! I have not decided which to give, so I shall give both! In order! With an interval for stew!
    - Three thirds of a bridge! Built over three years! The Table laughed for ten minutes, which I count as applause. Vane laughed too, and then quietly measured something. That is hope, *Player*!
    - Five words. I have them perfect now. I say them to Mags every night over the pot. She timed me at four breaths and one small extra speech. We are getting there. Not a word to Rivet!
    - What shall I tell you about, at length?
        - *Choice:* Tell me about the covered bridge.
        - *Choice:* Why do they call you Bellows?
        - *Choice:* How did you meet Mags?
        - *Choice:* What worries you?
        - *Choice:* Nothing, thanks.
    - Picture it! Lantern Square, a night of rain. The Night Market shuttered, buns soggy, Ladle's coals hissing. Now picture a roof over it all, a bridge from the Fiddler's Crossing to the far gutters, lanterns underneath, and every stall dry as a sermon!
    - I have drawings! I have costings! I have a speech on the dignity of a dry pepper bun! What I do not have is the Table's vote, and the timber, and, Vane tells me, a very great deal of sense. Two out of three is not bad!
    - The voice came first! My father was a Night Market crier; he could sell a stale bun across three streets. I learned to throw my voice off the fortress walls for fun. 'Bellows', they called me, and I thought: well, I had better make the nickname honest.
    - So I make bellows! For the forges, the kilns, the glass furnaces on the Row. Ferro's fire breathes through my leather, and so does Tinsel's. Every bellows comes with an opinion on last night's Table, free of charge.
    - Seventeen years ago I spent a whole winter praising her stew. In the middle of debates about other things. Drains. Lamp oil. A goat. I would stand up and say 'and furthermore, the stew', and the Table would groan.
    - She says she married me to stop me talking about it. She has not succeeded! It is the most persuasive campaign of my life, *Player*, and I won it with soup.
    - Worries? Me? I am never... hm. Close the door. Smaller voice. I worry the Table is too slow. Twenty years I have loved how slow it is. But the roads are worse every year, and Brindle needs volunteers, and something at the gate will not wait for us to finish.
    - So I end every speech with Brindle's call for volunteers now, whatever it began with. Bridges, lamp oil, the goat. 'And furthermore, the Watch.' It is the only thing I say that I never change my mind about.
    - Farewell, *Player*! Come to the Table! Bring an opinion! I shall disagree with it magnificently!
